title: Is This Massive New Study on the Benefits of Whole Grains Part of the “War on Protein” RFK Jr. is Ending? - Nautilus
gist: A European Heart Journal meta-analysis of 87 clinical trials links 4-6 daily whole-grain servings to significantly lower cardiovascular disease risk, cutting against HHS Secretary RFK Jr.'s protein-first inverted food pyramid.

insights.claim: A meta-analysis of 87 clinical trials published in the European Heart Journal found that eating four to six servings of whole-grain foods per day was associated with significantly reduced cardiovascular disease risk.
insights.speaker: Claire Maldarelli
insights.so_what: Supports demand narratives for whole-grain packaged foods and cereal makers versus protein-centric positioning.

insights.claim: The whole-grain/cardiovascular relationship appeared dose-dependent: the more whole grains people ate, the lower their apparent cardiovascular disease risk.

insights.so_what: Dose-response evidence strengthens health-claim marketing for grain-based products.
